text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Pechiney to sell rest of Carbone Lorraine stake. Carbone boss Claude Cocozza says sale is an "opportunity to make the shareholder base really international and better reflect the market reality of the group, which does 75 percent of its business outside France".
-- Pechiney announces three billion franc loss for 1996.
-- Thomson Multimedia announces 1996 loss of three billion francs as restructuring will mean 10,000 lay-offs.

-- CCF bank posts 1.4 billion franc profit, up 11.6 percent over 1995. Saint Louis posts 710 million franc net profit for 1996. Casino reports 838 million franc 1996 net profit. Promodes posts 1.24 billion franc net 1996 profit.
-- CAC 40 index briefly passes 2,700 mark for first time.
-- Renault's Schweitzer ready to sell doomed Vilvoorde facility to any competitor, adding he hopes the carmaker will break even by the end of the year.
-- European Commission chairman Jacques Santer suggests member countries have only one commissioner each. The current set-up gives big countries two.
-- BNP 1996 profits of 3.85 billion francs, double 1995 performance.
-- Utility supplier EDF posts 1.9 billion franc net 1996 profit.
-- Police question secretary general Jean-Francois Mancel of ruling RPR party "at his own request" in sleaze probe of Oise General Council.
-- U.S. and France agree to put off changing NATO's Southern Command, a key obstacle in talks to overhaul the alliance.
